body: Coverage in Belarus is limited to a single walking trekker in the historic centre of Minsk. The camera is lower than a normal car and is mostly on pedestrian roads.
The Minsk trekker showcases a historic part of the city with well-maintained classical European architecture. Many buildings have white or pastel-coloured walls.
The Holy Spirit Cathedral is a prominent landmark in the coverage. Its two towers can often be seen from a distance.
The pavement in the Minsk trekker consists mostly of grey rectangular tiles. A small section features pink-ish tiles in a specific pattern.
Signs are in either Belarusian or Russian, both of which use the Cyrillic alphabet.
Street signs in the center of Minsk are sea-green. The Cyrillic letters "вул (vul)", meaning street, can sometimes be seen.
